name: Blinq
summary: Digital business cards shared by QR code or link, with contacts syncing into your CRM.
best_for: teams and field-sales orgs that want consistent, branded digital cards with contacts syncing straight into the CRM — and events teams via the capture add-on
skip_if: you're an individual (the free tier honestly covers you), or your networking volume doesn't justify per-user pricing
honest_knock: The core product is honestly cheap — the cost that grows hides in event lead capture, now billed per lead at $9.99 a credit on top of the Business seats (read 7 October 2026), which is where teams that live on trade shows actually get value. And a truth about all digital cards: the wow factor works precisely because adoption is still low; the durable value is the CRM sync (contacts flowing automatically into your pipeline), so judge Business tier by that integration, not by the tap-to-share trick.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-08-17 and 2026-10-07) Free forever for individuals (2 cards, unlimited QR sharing). For individuals, Premium is $9.99 a month billed monthly or $7.33 billed annually. For teams, Business is $6.99 per user a month billed monthly or $4.99 per user billed annually, with a minimum charge of five cards, adding CRM sync, templates, the admin platform and team analytics; custom reporting sits on Enterprise. Enterprise is custom. Event lead capture is no longer a separate add-on: it is part of Business and billed per lead, 1 credit at $9.99 for each lead captured and enriched (0.75 credit when Blinq adds no email or phone, none for a duplicate), invoiced monthly in arrears on top of the seats; bulk and unlimited lead packages are quote-only. In August 2026 we recorded the add-on as starting around $199 a month (historical). Note the individual plan costs more per person than the team plan — if there are five of you, the team tier is both cheaper per head and more capable.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 on a free account, without a card and without importing contacts: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser through the web dashboard, without installing the app. We filled in a made-up card, shared it, opened the link in a separate browser without a Blinq login, changed the role and reloaded the same link.
findings: The web dashboard was enough to make and share a card: 'Finish setup' still asked for the app, but nothing we did needed it. The dashboard opened with a ready-made 'Work' card and two sample contacts from Blinq.

Share gives a short blinq.me link, a downloadable QR code, and sharing by email, iMessage and LinkedIn. Opened in a separate browser without a login, the link showed the card with name, role, company and 'Save Contact'.
After we changed the role to 'Research 2' and saved, reloading the same link showed the new role: no new link was needed.
Name, job title and company saved straight away ('Changes saved'). The website field, which requires a label, did not stay on the card in our attempt.

Starting a second card with + under Cards met no message or paywall (we did not save it). The free-choice theme colour carries a crown, so it is a Premium feature; lead capture and the contact scanner did not show up in the web dashboard.
You log in with your email address, but the card shows no email address unless you add one; we did not test this further.
not_tested: The mobile app, NFC and scanning the QR code with a phone
Actually saving a second card, and whether a limit appears then
Lead capture, the contact scanner and team features (paid)
What 'Save Contact' downloads on the recipient's side
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
